exposure: Mode of delivery (elective cesarean vs. vaginal birth) in women with a previous cesarean delivery
outcome: School achievement at age 8 (reading, writing, spelling, grammar, numeracy) categorised according to performing at above or ≤National Minimum Standards (NMS)
cohort: Children born in South Australia from 1999 to 2005
finding: There was little difference in school achievement at age 8 between children born by cesarean and vaginal birth after controlling for confounders.
mod_finding: Cesarean section did not increase the risk of poor school outcomes at age eight compared to vaginal birth in children of women with a previous cesarean delivery.
